Neros is transforming a defense industry mired in costly, behemoth machinery—to circumvent a looming vulnerability gap, to give dismounted soldiers a fighting chance against tanks, and ultimately, to get as many humans off the battlefield as possible.

While consumer technology is evolving by bounds on the smaller-cheaper-better path, U.S. defense technology wallows in the large, centralized, and wildly expensive paradigm. Our air, land, and sea machinery budget is staggering; yet these large assets can still be vulnerable to very small weapons. When swarm technology comes into its own, the asymmetry will escalate. Nowhere is the pattern more glaring than in small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS)—drones.

You'll work on one or more of our product lines, contributing to real mechanical design, testing, and manufacturing challenges that make an immediate impact. - Pursuing a BSE or MSE degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field

- Prior experience in fast paced engineering/manufacturing environments, including internships, co-ops, and/or project teams

- Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to solve problems through first principles thinking

- Experience with a CAD software such as Solidworks or NX

Nice to have

- Experience piloting, working with, or designing UAVs (including as a hobby!)

- Experience working in a high volume, cost sensitive industry like consumer electronics or automotive

- Broad knowledge of manufacturing processes and their appropriate applications

- Experience with packaging and integration of PCBAs, batteries, and RF components

- Familiarity with electrical and electromechanical components like BLDC motors and optical sensors

Design Architecture Engineer Intern

About the role

Astera Labs is seeking a Design Architecture Engineer Intern to help define complex ASIC and system designs from product requirements through implementation. You will work with architects and cross-functional engineering teams to develop clear architectural and microarchitectural specifications, evaluate design tradeoffs, and create the technical foundation for RTL, verification, physical design, DFT, and firmware.

You will gain hands-on experience turning system goals into block definitions, interfaces, dataflows, state machines, registers, clocking and reset behavior, performance budgets, and software-programming guidance. You will own a scoped architecture project with mentorship and present the resulting analysis, specification, and recommendations.

What you will do

- Review product requirements, system use cases, protocol specifications, and technical constraints to identify architecture needs and open questions.

- Develop or update architectural specifications describing major blocks, functions, interfaces, clocking, resets, software interactions, and system behavior.

- Create or refine microarchitecture specifications for blocks and subsystems, including logical implementation, data structures, programmable registers, state machines, datapaths, and dataflow diagrams.

- Define and analyze interface behavior, ownership, ordering, buffering, flow control, error handling, interrupts, and recovery sequences.

- Evaluate architecture tradeoffs involving latency, bandwidth, throughput, buffering, area, power, timing, scalability, complexity, and software impact.

- Build lightweight performance, capacity, traffic, or resource models using Python, spreadsheets, or comparable tools to support design decisions.

- Review address maps, CSR/register definitions, configuration options, clock and reset relationships, and programming requirements for consistency and completeness.

- Trace requirements into implementation and verification considerations; identify assumptions, corner cases, and measurable acceptance criteria.

- Participate in architecture, design, DV, physical-design, DFT, firmware, and program reviews; capture decisions, actions, risks, and unresolved items.

- Work with RTL, DV, PD, DFT, firmware, and systems engineers to clarify interfaces and improve the quality of handoff specifications.

- Support architecture-to-RTL and architecture-to-DV handoff by organizing specifications, diagrams, register collateral, review evidence, and verification guidance.

- Document the completed project, technical rationale, tradeoffs, open questions, and recommendations; present the results to engineering stakeholders.

What you bring

- Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

- Coursework, research, or project experience in computer architecture, digital systems, ASIC/FPGA design, embedded systems, high-speed interfaces, or hardware/software integration.

- Understanding of digital design concepts such as datapaths, state machines, registers, memory systems, interrupts, clocks, resets, and interfaces.

- Programming, scripting, or modeling experience with Python, C, C++, SystemVerilog, spreadsheets, or a comparable toolset.

- Ability to read technical specifications, organize complex information, reason about tradeoffs, and communicate precise technical decisions.

- Familiarity with Linux development environments, Git, technical documentation, diagrams, and collaborative review workflows.

- Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across engineering functions.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience writing architecture, microarchitecture, design, interface, protocol, or software-programming specifications.

- Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, UCIe, Ethernet, SerDes, chiplet, memory, or other high-speed interconnect architectures.

- Experience with performance modeling, bandwidth/latency analysis, traffic modeling, queue or buffer sizing, or resource budgeting.

- Exposure to RTL, design verification, formal methods, physical design, DFT, firmware, or system bring-up workflows.

- Familiarity with CSR and register-map design, address decoding, interrupt architecture, error reporting, telemetry, or debug infrastructure.

- Experience creating block diagrams, state diagrams, timing diagrams, interface tables, or traceability matrices.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Equal opportunity

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary:

Software Engineer Interns at PayPal develop innovative solutions and high-quality products that touch millions of people every day. Our engineers solve some of the most complex technical challenges in connected payments across multiple business units, including PayPal, Braintree, Venmo, and Paydiant. We are looking for candidates with exceptional technical talent, strong programming skills, and a keen desire to deeply understand our products and services while advancing our technology across functionality, performance, reliability, and scalability.

Job Description:

As a Software Engineer Intern, you will work alongside some of the best and brightest engineering talents in the industry. As an integral member of your team, you will estimate engineering efforts, design and implement solutions, test and deploy your changes, and help triage production issues. You should be dynamic, collaborative, and curious as we build new experiences, improve existing products, and develop distributed systems that power some of the world’s largest e-commerce and payments websites at a scale few companies can match.

Essential Responsibilities:

* Develop, test, debug, and maintain scalable front-end and/or back-end software using technologies such as Java, Python, Node.js, React, SQL, and REST APIs.

* Write clean, maintainable code; develop and optimize databases; and ensure data integrity and system performance.

* Follow software development life cycle (SDLC) processes, internal standards, coding conventions, and best practices while making technical decisions with appropriate guidance.

* Collaborate with managers, project leads, peers, and cross-functional partners—including design, product, and other business teams—to understand requirements and deliver effective solutions.

* Participate in code and design reviews and contribute to improving coding standards and development practices.

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

* Experience with at least one programming language, such as Java, Python, C++, JavaScript, or similar.

* Familiarity with software development concepts, including data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, and debugging.

* Experience developing projects through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects.

* Strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and analytical skills.

Internship Program Requirements:

* This is a Summer 2027 Internship program. Spring and Fall 2027 internships are not available.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship.

* Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field at an accredited college or university.

* Must be returning to school in Fall 2027.
* Applications will be accepted through Sunday, December 6th, 2026

IXL Learning, developer of personalized learning products used by millions of people globally, is seeking Software Engineer Interns who have a passion for technology and education. The IXL Engineering team is responsible for designing and creating the code that powers our amazing products.

As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll be involved in all aspects of the development process – including design, coding, testing, debugging, and tuning. We find it immensely satisfying to develop products that impact the lives of millions, and we are eager to have you join our team.

This is a full-time summer position in our San Mateo, CA headquarters office.

TECHNOLOGY

The technologies that we use include Java, Python, Typescript, AWS, React Native, Javascript, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Valkey.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Students in their third year of undergrad or students pursuing an advanced degree in Computer Science or a related discipline

- A solid grasp of general programming principles

- Excellent programming skills in Java or other object-oriented language

- Strong analytical-reasoning and problem-solving skills

- Ability to work both independently and in a wide variety of teams

- Knowledge of Java, SQL, JavaScript, CSS, source control is a plus

- Passion for improving education through technology

The pay rate for this position is $29 to $46 per hour.

IXL Learning is the country's largest EdTech company. We reach millions of learners through our diverse range of products. For example:

- 1 in 3 students in the United States uses IXL.com

- Rosetta Stone provides an immersive learning experience for 25 languages

- Wyzant is the nation's largest community of tutors, covering 300+ subjects

- Teachers Pay Teachers (TPT) is a comprehensive marketplace for millions of educator-created resources

Our mission is to create innovative products that will make a real, positive difference for learners and educators and we're looking for passionate, mission-minded people to join us in achieving this goal. We have a unique culture at IXL that fosters collaboration and the open exchange of ideas. We value our team and treat one another with kindness and respect. We approach our work with passion, tenacity, and authenticity. We find it immensely satisfying to develop products that impact the lives of millions and we are eager to have you join our team.

At IXL, we value diversity in age, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, physical and mental ability, political and religious beliefs, and life experience, and we are proud to promote a work environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work.
